title: Staggered comm-channel allocator and kernel-slicer to reduce TP comm/compute contention
author: Elena Park
description: Context: tensor-parallel workloads on multi-GPU crews occasionally observe long-tail stalls when collectives and compute kernels contend for the same GPU streams and host-to-device bandwidth. Motivation: reduce interleaved comm/compute contention and amortize small collective launches without increasing latency for critical microbatches. This PR implements a "staggered comm-channel allocator" and a lightweight "kernel-slicer" that together reshape how NCCL launches and kernel submissions are scheduled across streams to improve overlap and reduce NCCL queueing stalls. Summary of changes: 1) comm-channel allocator: introduce per-peer comm-channels with lease windows; allocator lazily assigns NCCL ranks to distinct streaming lanes based on active microbatch depth and observed bandwidth usage; supports backpressure thresholds and proactive lane defragmentation. 2) kernel-slicer: splits long GPU kernels into tail-resumable slices when they exceed configured runtime thresholds; slices are scheduled with affinity to compute lanes that avoid hot comm-channels. 3) Scheduler integration: scheduler now considers comm-lane affinity and slice boundaries when building microbatch launch plans; adds an optional prefer-comm-quiet-lane flag for low-p99 latency workloads. 4) Telemetry and knobs: new metrics (comm_lane_utilization, slice_preempt_count, comm_wait_ms) and runtime flags to tune lease_window_ms and slice_runtime_target_ms; CGroup-friendly limits to avoid starvation. 5) Tests and docs: unit tests for allocator invariants, microbench harness for TP kernels, and docs describing operational knobs and rollout guidance. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1829) - [x] microbench harness added - [x] unit + integ tests - [x] perf numbers validated on internal clusters - [x] canary rollout plan included Performance summary: on 8xA100-80GB TP runs with 1k/2k token distributions, end-to-end tokens/sec improved +12.8% on average, p95 latency reduced by 9.7% for interactive microbatch sizes, KV-cache miss-induced stalls decreased by 22% for workloads with frequent KV invalidation; observed slice_preempt_count was low (<0.6 per 1k requests) with default thresholds. Rollout plan: canary to 10% of Dedicated GPU pools, monitor comm_lane_utilization and comm_wait_ms for five days, progressively increase to 100% with automated rollback on >5% regressions in p95 or increase in error rates. Backwards compatibility: allocator is opt-in via prefer-staggered-comm runtime flag; kernel-slicer enabled by default for kernels > slice_runtime_target_ms. Related work: follows up on ENG-1523 (KV-prefetch heuristics) and complements previous NCCL pacing efforts; references design notes in Linear ENG-1901. Migration notes: no model changes required, operator should ensure driver and NCCL versions are compatible with stream priority semantics (NVIDIA driver >= 525, NCCL >= 2.14 recommended).

release_notes: Improves tensor-parallel comm/compute overlap by introducing a staggered comm-channel allocator and kernel slicing. Expect ~10-15% throughput gains on multi-GPU TP workloads and reduced p95 latency in interactive use-cases.
review_comments: Mateo Silva: Nice approach. Two requests: add a guard to prevent lease thrashing under very high microbatch depth, and include a brief benchmark for the pathological case where all peers contend on one lane.
Elena Park (author): Added lease backoff and demo benchmark for pathological peer fan-in in latest commit; results logged in bench output.
Priya Raman: Can we make the slice_runtime_target_ms default conservative? Suggest 8ms instead of 4ms for now to avoid preemption overheads.
Elena Park: Updated default to 8ms and added runtime knob to lower it for aggressive perf experiments.
Gordon Liu: Verified no regressions on 4-GPU small models and approve.
benchmarks: KV-cache miss stall reduction: -22% (workloads with frequent KV invalidation)
deployment_notes: Canary to Dedicated clusters (10%) for 72h with enhanced telemetry, watch comm_lane_utilization and comm_wait_ms; runtime flag prefer-staggered-comm=true to enable allocator, kernel-slicer can be toggled via slice_runtime_target_ms; rollback: revert flag and re-deploy scheduler binary.
test_instructions: Run tests: pytest tests/tp/test_allocator.py::TestAllocator and tests/tp/test_kernel_slicer.py::TestSlicer; run perf harness: python benchmarks/tp/staging/prefetch_latency.py --runs 50 --workers 4; compare metrics with baseline via perf/compare.py baseline.json current.json.
notes: This PR focuses on reducing microbatch-level NCCL contention patterns observed in production. Operators should pair this with NCCL tune and node-level link-rate smoothing for best results.
